article.opening: Mars enters Pisces on {{entryDate}} after moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, and action starts following feeling rather than a fixed route. We help before anyone asks. We follow an idea before we can explain it. A task that nobody claimed gets done because someone senses what is needed and quietly begins.
article.tension: That sensitivity can keep action moving, but it can also hide the point where willingness ends. We take on the extra piece without naming a limit, soften an answer until no one knows what was decided, and avoid the conversation that might disappoint someone. The work still gets done for a while. Then energy scatters across too many needs, the original aim gets harder to find, and anger comes out as a canceled plan, a sharp aside, or silence after another automatic yes.
article.development: Mars last moved through Pisces from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}. This pass brings the same pressure back into view: compassion without a boundary keeps creating obligations that nobody clearly chose. We may start with one useful act, notice three more needs, and spend the day responding to whatever feels most urgent. A creative impulse can dissolve under constant interruption. A real disagreement can stay unnamed while its heat moves into unrelated moments. By the time the limit is obvious, the original desire has been buried under favors, guesses, and repairs.
article.close: By {{exitDate}}, repeated unplanned favors can leave the original desire untouched and the anger aimed at whoever asks next.
try_this: We can choose one request this week and say exactly which part we can take on.
We can give one creative impulse thirty uninterrupted minutes and make a rough first version.
We can name one irritation in a plain sentence before doing another favor around it.
